notes: One contract on Ethereum mainnet (chain id 1): MarginaliaAnnex (src/MarginaliaAnnex.sol). Constructor (address hook, address intake, bytes32 action, address signer), in declaration order: hook = 0xf0457dd0cf526686190e4f057ba19db14d34a0cc, the live MarginaliaHook of launch 1283; intake = 0x1397434cd35e8a9C8aC312A61D3A285EB31dea56, the IdentityMD Intake; action = bytes32('oracle.request@oracle-1') = 0x6f7261636c652e72657175657374406f7261636c652d31 right-padded with zeros, the oracle action; signer = 0x5598Aa9146215Bc13eb26f2c692Ad1461Fd32982, the IdentityMD oracle signer. These are the same constants the live hook holds as INTAKE, ACTION and ORACLE_SIGNER. The constructor reads no chain state and makes no external call; it stores hook, intake and action as immutables and hands the signer to OracleAttestationConsumer (EIP-712 domain IdentityMD Oracle v2). No owner, pause or upgrade exists, so $owner is not used and no privileged argument is passed; the factory as msg.sender gets no role. No token, pool, funding or initialization call. What it does: Marginalia calls (falsifiable price calls with a bond) on the Uniswap v4 pools the hook's immutable router cannot accept, chiefly every IMD custom_token launch pool behind the factory's PoolInitializationGuard hook 0x784ff9a3ac5d88a30bfff6f7f2a270161fbe6000 (address bits 0x2000, beforeInitialize only). Venue rule: a live v4 pool with X on one side and IMD 0xD34a99Bc0f67aE1bbd63C660e6d0b0dd03E263B7 / WETH / native on the other whose hook is none or the Marginalia hook, has no swap permission bits (BEFORE_SWAP, AFTER_SWAP, BEFORE_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA, AFTER_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA read from the address; a dynamic-fee pool, fee 0x800000, passes only with the Marginalia hook or an admitted hook), or was admitted permanently by the IdentityMD oracle panel: requestAdmission(address[] hooks) takes 1 to MAX_ADMISSION_LIST 4 hooks with code, pays the Intake's current price for the action (refused above MAX_PRICE 1 IMD), builds the question itself (answerType address[], panelSize 5, quorum 4, guards.allow = the list, consumer = this contract) and buys one answer; onOracleResult accepts only the Intake, verifies the attestation against the signer, requires chainId == block.chainid, agreed >= quorum >= 4 and panelSize >= 5, consumes the request id once and admits only hooks both asked about and named. Economics: post(params, v4Key, bond, minMargOut, baselineBound, deadline) pulls STAMP 0.1 + MARG_BUY 0.25 + bond (BOND_MIN 0.25 <= bond <= BOND_MAX 10) in IMD from the author; one swap of 0.35 IMD on the hook's MARG/IMD pool through the hook's PoolManager (unlockCallback accepts only the PoolManager): the 0.25 share of the MARG goes to the author (bounded by minMargOut), the 0.10 share to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD (Burned); the bond is held as IMD. Same rules as the hook: targetBps >= 10% from par on the call's side, horizon 1-90 days, text 1-280 bytes, class Agent when the author has code else Declared, checkpointVenue windows through the immutable stateless MarginaliaPricer 0xEaff9B262341A0cB05579227e662BFE768A71cfb (first checkpoint 1 to 6 hours old), observe(id) in [horizonEnd, +6h] with 3 to 16 readings 20 blocks apart spanning an hour, hold rule on BUY, settle(id) after the window with the most adverse reading deciding: RIGHT returns the bond via claimDeposit, WRONG / VOID_SOLD forfeit it to the hook's pools through hook.fundPot with KEEPER_BPS 10% to the settler, VOID_NODATA returns it and scores as wrong, retract(id, text) before the horizon forfeits the whole bond and scores minus half. Score is difficulty-weighted reputation only. Counter-calls may target an open call here or on the hook via hook.noteOf. Ids keccak(annex, n); records(wallet); reads noteOf, venueOf, observationsOf. nonReentrant on post/settle/retract/claim/admission/callback. Checked on this tree: forge build passes, forge test --match-path test/Annex.t.sol passes 29 of 29, runtime 24,493 bytes, under EIP-170.
